nodes.summary: The set of biunitary divisors of $0$ is empty.
nodes.title: Zero has no biunitary divisors

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, the biunitary divisors of $n$ are the divisors $d$ of $n$ with $\gcd_1(d, n/d) = 1$, where $\gcd_1(a, b)$ denotes the greatest common unitary divisor of $a$ and $b$. For $n = 0$ the set is empty.
nodes.title: Biunitary divisors

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $d$, if $d$ is a biunitary divisor of $n$, then $d$ divides $n$.
nodes.title: Biunitary divisors divide

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $a$ and $b$, the greatest common unitary divisor satisfies $\gcd_1(a, b) = \gcd_1(b, a)$.
nodes.title: Symmetry of the greatest common unitary divisor

nodes.summary: For positive natural numbers $a$ and $b$, the greatest common unitary divisor $\gcd_1(a, b)$ divides $a$.
nodes.title: The greatest common unitary divisor divides its first argument

nodes.summary: For positive natural numbers $a$ and $b$, the greatest common unitary divisor $\gcd_1(a, b)$ divides $b$.
nodes.title: The greatest common unitary divisor divides its second argument

nodes.summary: For positive natural numbers $a$ and $b$, the greatest common unitary divisor $\gcd_1(a, b)$ is a unitary divisor of $a$ and a unitary divisor of $b$.
nodes.title: The greatest common unitary divisor is a common unitary divisor

nodes.summary: For positive natural numbers $a$ and $b$, the greatest common unitary divisor $\gcd_1(a, b)$ is positive.
nodes.title: Positivity of the greatest common unitary divisor

nodes.summary: For every natural number $b$, the greatest common unitary divisor satisfies $\gcd_1(0, b) = 0$, since $0$ has no unitary divisors.
nodes.title: Greatest common unitary divisor with zero on the left

nodes.summary: For every natural number $a$, the greatest common unitary divisor satisfies $\gcd_1(a, 0) = 0$, since $0$ has no unitary divisors.
nodes.title: Greatest common unitary divisor with zero on the right

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $a$ and $b$, $\gcd_1(a, b)$ is the largest natural number that is a unitary divisor of both $a$ and $b$, where a unitary divisor of $n$ is a divisor $d$ of $n \neq 0$ with $\gcd(d, n / d) = 1$. If $a = 0$ or $b = 0$, there is no common unitary divisor and $\gcd_1(a, b) = 0$.
nodes.title: Greatest common unitary divisor

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $a$, $b$ and $d$, if $d$ is a unitary divisor of both $a$ and $b$, then $d \le \gcd_1(a, b)$, where $\gcd_1(a, b)$ is the greatest common unitary divisor of $a$ and $b$.
nodes.title: Common unitary divisors are at most the greatest one

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $d$, $d$ is a biunitary divisor of $n$ if and only if $d$ divides $n$, $n \neq 0$ and $\gcd_1(d, n / d) = 1$, where $\gcd_1$ denotes the greatest common unitary divisor.
nodes.title: Characterization of biunitary divisors

nodes.summary: The sum $\sigma^{**}(4)$ of the biunitary divisors of $4$ equals $5$.
nodes.title: The biunitary divisor sum of $4$

nodes.summary: The sum $\sigma^{**}(120)$ of the biunitary divisors of $120$ equals $3 \cdot 120 = 360$.
nodes.title: $120$ is biunitary triperfect

nodes.summary: The sum $\sigma^{**}(1)$ of the biunitary divisors of $1$ equals $1$.
nodes.title: The biunitary divisor sum of $1$

nodes.summary: The sum $\sigma^{**}(16)$ of the biunitary divisors of $16$ equals $1 + 2 + 8 + 16 = 27$.
nodes.title: The biunitary divisor sum of $16$

nodes.summary: The sum $\sigma^{**}(27)$ of the biunitary divisors of $27$ equals $1 + 3 + 9 + 27 = 40$.
nodes.title: The biunitary divisor sum of $27$

nodes.summary: The sum $\sigma^{**}(0)$ of the biunitary divisors of $0$ equals $0$.
nodes.title: The biunitary divisor sum of $0$

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, $\sigma^{**}(n)$ is the sum of the biunitary divisors of $n$, that is, of the divisors $d$ of $n$ with $\gcd_1(d, n / d) = 1$, where $\gcd_1$ denotes the greatest common unitary divisor. Since $0$ has no biunitary divisors, $\sigma^{**}(0) = 0$.
nodes.title: Biunitary divisor sum

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
